title: Anatomy, Physiology, and Neurology of the Speech Mechanism
description: Anatomical, physiological, and neurological bases for an understanding of speech communication.

title: Aural Anatomy and Pathology
description: Anatomy and physiology of the normal human auditory system; causes and types of hearing impairment; otological considerations medical and surgicalimplications.

title: Assessment and Rehabilitation for Hearing-Impaired Adults
description: Introduction to psychoacoustic principles as applied to audiometric diagnostics and aural rehabilitation with adults.

title: Amplification for the Hearing Impaired
description: Covers methodology for rehabilitating persons with hearing loss; emphasizesrecent developments in instrumentation and measurement techniques. Hearing aids and real-ear analysis are used with hands-on laboratory approach. Emphasizes interfacing amplification to the patient and family.

title: Assessment and Treatment of Child Phonologic Disorders
description: A study of principle and methods for assessing children's speech productionto determine existence of phonologic disorders and a review of varieties oftreatment methods for such disorders.
prerequisites_raw: Speech and Hearing Sciences 50, 120, 166, and Linguistics 137.

title: Principles of Behavior Modification
description: Basic principles of operant conditioning and their use in classroom, family, and clinical environments with special reference to speech-language pathology.

title: Introduction to Stuttering
description: Review and analysis of the features and characteristics of stuttering, the areas and causes of stuttering, conditions that modify stuttering, and current therapies for stuttering.

title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Independent work with faculty sponsor culminating in senior thesis.

title: Group Studies for Advanced Students
description: Selected topics in accordance with instructor's area of specialization.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

title: Instructional Laboratory
description: Tutoring experience for advanced undergraduate students in preparation for graduate education.

title: Independent Studies
description: Independent studies.

title: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in accordance with instructors' specializations.

title: Russian Culture
description: Analyzes crucial trends and issues in Russian culture in their historical, social, and technological settings, from the rise of Moscow in the fifteenth century to post-Soviet Russia. All lectures and readings are in English.

title: Short Fiction by Major Russian Writers
description: Survey of short fiction by major Russian short story writers such as Gogol, Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Chekhov, Bunin, Babel, Nabokov, Petrushevskaya, and Pelevin. Analyzes short story as form and examines works in literary and cultural context. Lectures and readings in English.Designed for first and second year students.

title: Introduction to Research
description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member. Exceptional students are offered an opportunity to undertake independent or collaborative research or to act as interns for faculty-directed research projects.

title: Great Russian Writers
description: Intensive study of one author. Readings supplemented by select criticism. Readings and lectures in English. Pushkin, Gogol, Leskov, Turgenev, Goncharov, Chekhov, Dostoevsky,Tolstoy, Nabokov, Bulgakov

title: Pushkin
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism.Taught in English.

title: Gogol
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism.Taught in English.

title: Leskov
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism.Taught in English.

title: Turgenev

title: Goncharov
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism.Taught in English.

title: Chekhov
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism.Taught in English.

title: Dostoevsky
description: Intensive study of Dostoevsky. Readings supplemented by select criticism. Readings and lectures in English.

title: Tolstoy
description: Intensive study of Tolstoy. Readings supplemented by select criticism. Readings and lectures in English.

title: Nabokov
description: Intensive study of Nabokov. Readings supplemented by select criticism. Readings and lectures in English.

title: Bulgakov
description: Intensive study of one writer. Readings supplemented by selected criticism. Taught in English.

title: Russian Drama
description: Plays from the classic, romantic, and realistic periods; Chekhov's innovative works, as well as dramas represntative of various trends before and after 1917. Readings and discussion in English.

title: Nineteenth-Century Russian Literature I
description: Introduction to Russian literary culture from 1800 to 1850. Readings by Pushkin, Lermontov, Gogol, Dostoevsky, and others. Readings is English.

title: Nineteenth-Century Russian Literature II
description: Introduction to Russian literary culture from 1850 to 1900. Readings by Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Goncharov, Turgenev, Leskov, Saltykov-Shchedrin, Chekhov. Taught in English.

title: Twentieth-Century Russian Literature I
description: Intensive study of particular authors, genres, literary movements, and selected topics in Russian literature from 1900-1954. Taught in English.

title: Twentieth-Century Russian Literature II
description: Intensive study of particular authors, genres, literary movements, and selected topics in Russian literature after World War II. Taught in English.

title: The Avantgarde in Russia
description: The Russian Avantgarde in its European context. The avantgarde and the revolution of 1917. Analysis of key figures and movements within the Russian Avantgarde. Taught in English.

title: Russian Cinema
description: Introduction to the development of Soviet cinema from the early days to thepresent. A focal point will be the interaction between politics/ideology and film in Russia. Major directors such as Eisenshtein and Tarkovski will be treated extensively. Readings and lectures in English.

title: Contemporary Art in Russia and Eastern Europe
description: Study of central intellectual and aesthetic trends in the late Soviet period and in contemporary post-Soviet Russia and Eastern Europe. Analysis of literary texts and the visual arts. Taught in English.

title: Russian Art
description: Introduction to Russian art and aesthetic theory from the beginning to the present. Readings and lectures in English.

title: Masters of Soviet Cinema
description: Introduction to some of the great directors in Russian cinema. Analysis of films and theoretical writings. Study of key theoretical concepts. Taught in English. E. Eisenshtein.

title: Eighteenth-Century Culture
description: Introduction to eighteenth-century Russian literature, philosophy, and the visual arts. Taught in English.
